title: deriveFactId's hash material uses an unescaped "|" delimiter (`${studentId}|${key}|${canonicalJson(value)}|${sessionId ?? root_cause: src/erasure.ts:462-489: the read-back loop computes totalRemaining as the SUM of 9 sequential, independently-awaited countDocuments calls (one per ERASURE_PLAN step), evaluated only AFTER the whole loop finishes. title: with the shipped default ERASURE_FENCE_GRACE_MS = 0, a fence-aware writer whose post-write check (compensateIfFenced) runs AFTER the fence's own release at completion is not caught: its write survives, the erasure's receipt falsely reports verified:true / totalRemaining:0 / status:completed, and studentId + carriedSelectors are unset on that same commit, so there is no automated retry path -- the orphaned personal data is permanent unless a brand-new erasure request is manually filed for the same student
source: checker cycle 2, own hostile probe (THE KEY PROBE, checker brief item 3)
reproduction: seedTwo() (real applyApprovedDiff-seeded student). Pause a real applyApprovedDiff writer at its own facts.insertOne (after its pre-check passes, since the pre-check would otherwise refuse it once the fence exists -- this is the only way a writer's insert can land at all). requestErasure + confirmErasure (sets the fence). Hook erasure_fences.deleteMany (the call releaseErasureFence makes for grace<=0) to, AFTER the real delete removes the fence document, release the paused writer and await its completion. Call executeErasure(db, requestId). Result: out.status === 'completed', out.receipt.verified === true, the writer's applyApprovedDiff call resolves { ok: true } (not StudentFencedError), and its fact + 2 edges are present in the fake collections afterward. A second executeErasure(db, requestId) call on the same request returns alreadyCompleted:true with the SAME stale receipt (totalRemaining:0) without re-scanning, and the row's studentId is already unset -- confirmed via a standalone repro script (zz-ckr2-permanence.mjs, run via npx tsx, deleted before commit) that the orphaned fact is still physically present after two executeErasure calls with no automated way to find it again.
root_cause: D-015's fence-plus-compensation design guarantees closure only for a writer W whose post-check runs WHILE the fence is up (W sees it and self-compensates) or whose writes all landed before the fence existed (so the purge's own resolve, which runs strictly after the fence is set, finds and deletes them). Neither disjunct covers a writer whose ENTIRE write completed before the fence, or straddles it, but whose post-check (a separate async DB round trip, isStudentFenced -> erasure_fences.findOne) is scheduled to run only after completion + release. With the default grace of 0, that window opens the instant the completion CAS commits -- there is no synchronization forcing every in-flight writer's post-check to run before that instant. This is documented by the maker as a known residual (manifest 'Fix cycle 2' Residuals section, and gate erasure-fencing Q1), but is shipped as the DEFAULT (ERASURE_FENCE_GRACE_MS = 0), not merely a configurable option a caller must opt into.
judgment: checker's ruling on item 3's question: a non-zero technical grace period (at least as long as the slowest fence-aware writer can realistically take) is REQUIRED for the fence mechanism to deliver B15's guarantee ('a verification pass reads back every collection and proves zero documents remain for that student') -- independent of the re-enrolment policy question gate erasure-fencing Q1 asks. Q1 frames grace length as a re-enrolment/UX tradeoff ('how long before this student can be written again'); this probe shows grace also does load-bearing CORRECTNESS work (closing the release-boundary race), which is a technical requirement the Approver's policy answer does not get to set to zero without reopening this exact gap. Shipping grace=0 as the default, with the request permanently losing its retry key (studentId, carriedSelectors) on completion, means B15's stated guarantee is provably false for this window, with no automated way to ever detect or recover the orphan.
fix: for fix cycle 3 (last cycle): either (a) ship a safe non-zero default grace bounded by a documented maximum writer duration (the existing gate erasure-fencing Q1 recommendation of 24h already covers this, so answering Q1 non-zero and changing ERASURE_FENCE_GRACE_MS's default closes this without new mechanism), or (b) do not unset studentId/carriedSelectors and do not treat the row as un-retryable at the instant of the completion CAS -- keep the retry key until AFTER the grace-delayed release has also passed a final confirmation read-back, so a completed-but-still-orphaned request can still be found and swept even at grace=0.

Same failure class (unhandledRejection under Node's default policy, >=15, crashes the process) the ISS-t-015-c0-3 fix was written to close; only the synchronous half is closed. The shipped default (defaultSweepErrorLogger) is synchronous and does not exhibit this.

title: startErasureFenceSweep's tick() cycle-1 fix (erasure.ts, for ISS-t-017-rev-2/ISS-t-017-c0-1) makes the outer `.catch(...).finally(() => { inFlight = false })` WAIT for onError's own returned promise chain to settle -- correct for the sync-throw and async-reject cases, but if onError returns a promise that NEVER settles (neither resolves nor rejects -- e.g. an async logging call with no timeout, hung on a stuck connection, exactly the documented/encouraged usage 'a caller SHOULD pass one wired to its logging'), the whole chain never settles either, so `.finally()` NEVER RUNS. `inFlight` is never reset to false, and every subsequent tick silently no-ops (`if (inFlight) return;`) -- forever, for the remaining life of the process, not just the failing tick. Empirically confirmed (scratch probe): onError was called exactly once; across 4 further ticks it was never called again -- the sweep is dead. Directly contradicts the code's own docstring ('so one bad tick never kills the interval OR the process'). No crash, no unhandledRejection, no log line, and nothing in this codebase monitors sweep liveness -- a silent, permanent halt of the B15 erasure-fence release mechanism. The shipped default (apps/api/src/index.ts defaultSweepErrorLogger) is a synchronous console.error and is not exposed; reachable only once a caller wires an async onError without an internal timeout, which is the documented usage pattern.
